Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa! I contemplate that Supreme Ego (Parāhaṃtā), which is my own self-manifest form, the unsurpassed one, in whom this entire universe shines forth like the sprout from a seed. (1) Having bowed to the lotus feet of the venerable Pādavānanda, who resides in my heart, I shall bring forth this "Wish-fulfilling Tree of Good Fortune" (Saubhāgyakalpadruma), which grants all desires. (2)

(3) "I shall meditate upon that Mother in my heart, who is always worshipped by the lords of practitioners through morning recollections, ritual bathing, twilight prayers, japa, nyāsa, and other rites.
Then, having arisen from his seat, the lord of practitioners, while contemplating his own deity, sits with one-pointed mind upon a stable lotus-seat or similar posture.
Visualizing Śrīnātha—who resembles the full moon—seated within the pericarp of a clear, thousand-petaled lotus facing downward on the crown of his head, he [focuses] upward at the mūlādhāra.

Having meditated upon Kuṇḍalinī— who resides within the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus of the mouth, who resembles a sleeping serpent, who has the form of three and a half coils, who is as subtle as a lotus fiber, and whose tip shines like lightning— and having visualized her awakened by the breath of *kumbhaka* as entering through the path of the Suṣumṇā into the lunar orb situated in the Brahma-randhra, reaching a state of oneness therein, and being flooded by streams of nectar flowing from that lunar orb;

Meditating upon oneself, preceded by the placement (*nyāsa*) of the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*, one should contemplate the sandals (*pādukā*). Then, having worshipped with the five mental offerings (*upacāra*) as follows: "Laṃ, to the Earth-nature, I offer fragrance; Haṃ, to the Space-nature, flowers; Yaṃ, to the Air-nature, incense; Raṃ, to the Fire-nature, a lamp; Vaṃ, to the Nectar-nature, food offering (*naivedya*)," and having offered praise beginning with "In the Brahma-aperture," etc., preceded by the display of the five mudrās, [one should contemplate] the primordial Śakti emerging from the lunar orb.

Having meditated on the form described above within the unstruck lotus (*anāhata-kamala*) and having worshipped it with mental offerings according to one's capacity, one should mentally recite the Vidyā while meditating as before upon the *mūlādhāra*.

Having performed worship with the five offerings (*pañcopacāra*), one should praise the Guru and the Deity with hymns and then attend to the necessary duties. Then, having bathed appropriately at a sacred ford (*tīrtha*) or similar place, [one should offer oblations]:
*Raṃ ātma-tattvāya svāhā* (1); *Klīṃ vidyā-tattvāya* (2); *Hrīṃ śiva-tattvāya svāhā* (3). *Raṃ sauḥ śivata...* [end of fragment].

Hā (3) sarvataḥ-hā (4). Having wiped the lips and washed the hands, one should perform the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*). This [procedure] should be understood as necessary at the beginning of all rites. Having inhaled air through the left nostril with the ring finger, little finger, and thumb, and having mentally recited the *mūla-mantra*, one should exhale through the other [nostril]; thus one performs breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). Then, having noted the place and time and described the eight-limbed posture (*aṣṭāṅga-sthiti*), one makes the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "For the pleasure of the Supreme Deity, I shall perform the bath. Having immersed oneself three times in the water, [one stands] in front of oneself in the water...

Having formed a triangle with its apex facing upward, having placed the *vāla* seed-syllable from the tip toward the left, and having likewise placed the *māyā* syllable in the center; then, having visualized the deity in the center, one should worship it with "Oṃ, salutation to Earth" (*laṃ pṛthivyai namaḥ*) and so forth. Then, [one should recite]: "O Sun, by that truth that the holy fords (*tīrthas*) within the belly of the cosmic egg are touched by your rays, grant me the holy ford (*tīrtha*). Having drawn the holy ford from the solar disc with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* while reciting "Krom," having invoked [the deity] therein, and having rendered it nectar with the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting "Vam," [one should proceed].

Having sprinkled [the water] seven times on the head with the *mūla-mantra* while performing the *guṣṭhānāmāyoga*, and having consecrated the forehead, heart, and arms three times each with the *kuṃbha-mudrā*, one should remain submerged there in the water while reciting the *mūla-mantra*. Having meditated upon the deity as being of the nature of the sacred ford (*tīrtha*), one should rise, perform the triple ablution (*trirnimajja*), sip water (*ācamya*), put on two garments, and sit upon the seat. Having sipped water again and covered the ashes in the left hand with the right, one should recite: "I take refuge in Sadyojāta; obeisance to Sadyojāta. In Bhava... [and so forth].

Salutation to the one who transcends existence, beyond existence, the self-existence, and the source of existence. Salutation to Vāmadeva; salutation to Jyeṣṭha; salutation to Śreṣṭha; salutation to Rudra; salutation to Kāla; salutation to Kalavikaraṇa; salutation to Balavikaraṇa; salutation to Bala; salutation to Balapramathana;

salutation to Sarvabhūtadamana; salutation to Manonmana. To those who are not terrible, to those who are terrible, and to those more terrible than the terrible—to all of them, to all the Śarvas, salutation!

"May there be Rudra in the form of the Master (Maheśvara). We know that Tatpuruṣa; we meditate upon Mahādeva; may that Rudra inspire us. Īśāna is the lord of all sciences, the sovereign of all beings, the overlord of Brahman, the overlord of the Veda; may the auspicious Brahman be mine, the eternal Śiva—Oṃ. Having recited this mantra of Kāmeśvara, and having thus consecrated [the object] with the five mantras beginning with Īśāna and with the *praṇava* (Oṃ) on the head, forehead, heart, hands, feet, and all limbs, one should sprinkle [it].

Having applied *tilaka* with sandalwood paste, one should draw the triple mark (*tripuṇḍra*) on the forehead and other parts of the body. Then, having sipped water (*ācamana*) and performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) as before: "I shall perform the morning twilight worship (*prātaḥ-saṃdhyā*). Having performed the meditation beginning with the *mūla-mantra* and ending with the visualization, one should take water held in the right hand covered by the left, and recite the four seed-syllables—*Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*—followed by the five elemental seed-syllables—*Laṃ Vaṃ Raṃ Yaṃ Haṃ*—and the *Amṛtamālinī-vidyā*: *Mūla-saptāvṛtti Amṛtamālinī Svāhā*.

Having consecrated [the water] seven times with the mantra, one should take it in the left hand and, by the union of the right thumb and ring finger, sprinkle it seven times on the head and the heart with the root-mantra. Then, having contemplated the remaining water as being of the nature of light (*tejas*), and having united it with the nectar of the *kula*, one should visualize it entering through the right nostril, washing away all impurities within, and exiting through the other [left] nostril; then, taking it with the right hand, one should place it in one's own left [hand].

O Bhairava, I satiate your sandals, namaḥ," one should meditate upon [the deity] at the *mūlādhāra* as having a luster equal to ten million flashes of lightning. Then, by means of the sequence for invoking that radiance, having invoked [the deity] externally into the fire-mandala in the sky, one should meditate upon Vāgīśvarī arising therefrom, as follows: yellow, clad in yellow garments, and adorned with yellow unguents and garlands.

One should meditate upon Vāgbhavī, who is adorned with various ornaments, whose splendor is equal to ten million flashes of lightning, who is radiant with a rosary of *akṣa* seeds, who holds a book and a lotus in her hands, who sits upon a seat of fire, who has arisen from the *vāgbhava* syllable, who possesses three eyes, and who wears a beautiful smile. (1-2) Having thus meditated and worshipped her with the *mānasopacāras*, [one should recite]: "Aiṃ! We know the Goddess Tripurā; we meditate upon the Mistress of Speech; may Muktikā, the Mistress of Speech, inspire us. (3-4) Aiṃ! O Pādukā of the Mistress of Speech!...

Then, having performed the dismissal of the deity (*udvāsana*) and completed the worship of the *ṛṣi* and other [limbs], one should recite the root *Gāyatrī*, or the root *Vāgbhava-Gāyatrī*, or the *Vāgbhava-bīja* ten times each. Having performed the worship with "Obeisance to the Sky" (*me vyoman*) and having sipped water (*ācamya*), one should offer [the prayer] with "May this morning twilight be dear to the Supreme Deity. Having performed the placement of the hands (*nyāsa*) up to its conclusion and having offered the leaf (*parṇa*) with the *arghya* of the Root Deity, one should recite the Root Gāyatrī ten times. Even during a period of ritual impurity (*āśauca*), only this much is required; however, the utterance of the mantra must be mental. Thus, having performed the morning twilight worship, one should recite the Vidyā of the Lord of that day and the Ghaṭikā-vidyā thirty-eight times.
Having performed the worship of the deities beginning with Mūla and ending with Ṛṣi, etc., as prescribed: (1) *Mū-aṃ-ṛṃ haṃ prakāśātmaka-mananyā-śānandanātha-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ* (1|4).

In this manner, after the recitation of the respective Lord’s Vidyā and the recitation of the Ghaṭikā-vidyā, one should repeat the Root-mantra sixteen times and sixty times respectively. When performing the Pārāyaṇa of the Lord and the Ghaṭikā, this [root-repetition] must be performed; that Pārāyaṇa is now described in its full scope. Next is the Midday Sandhyā:

from the Ācamana up to the libation (tarpaṇa) to Mārtaṇḍa-Bhairava, the procedure is the same as before, except that the word "midday" (madhyāhna) should be substituted for the word "morning" (prātaḥ) in the formal resolve (saṃkalpa). Thereafter...

Having meditated upon the *hate*-*klīṃ* seed-syllable, which is red in color, as before, one should invoke [it] into the solar disc in the sky and meditate upon Kāmeśvarī, who has arisen from it. As follows: "One should contemplate Kāmeśvarī—red, richly adorned with garments and ornaments, holding a noose, a goad, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons, possessing a pure smile, endowed with the vigor of youth, and having three eyes. Having thus meditated and worshipped her mentally, [one recites]: *klīṃ tripurādevīṃ vidmahe*.

"Kāmeśvarī, we meditate upon; may that Klinnā inspire us. Having offered the *arghya* three times with "Kāmeśvarī-pādukāyai," and having satiated [the deity] three times with "Klīṃ Kāmeśvarī-yai," the remaining procedures such as the sipping of water (*ācamana*) are the same. At the place where the recitation of the *Vāgbhava-gāyatrī* seed-syllable occurs, the specific difference is the recitation of the *Kāma-gāyatrī* seed-syllable. One should offer the *sandhyā* as before. Thus, having performed the midday *sandhyā*, for that day...

Having thus recited the Vidyās of the respective elements and directions three times each, one should repeat the Root Mantra thirty-six times. In this context, the recitation of the respective mantras should be placed at the beginning of the names, such as Kāmeśvarī and so forth.
It is said: here too, it should be understood that this [rite] must be performed when the *pārāyaṇa* (recitation) is not being carried out. Now, regarding the evening twilight (*sāyaṃ-saṃdhyā*):

there too, having substituted the word "evening" (*sāyam*) in the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*), and having performed the ritual up to the libation (*tarpaṇa*) for Bhairava, one should visualize the seed-syllable *sauḥ* as white in color within the *ājñā-cakra*.

Then, as before, having invoked her from the lunar orb in the sky, one should meditate upon Amṛteśvarī, who has arisen from that [orb]: white, adorned with white garments, unguents, garlands, and ornaments, wearing a mass of matted hair (*jaṭājūṭa*), and possessing three eyes.

In the tradition of the Thirty Nityās, there is a daily recitation (*japa*) following the daily obligatory recitation; however, in the tradition of the Sixteen Nityās, it should be understood that this applies only to the final one. This should be known as the procedure when the *Nityā-pārāyaṇa* is not being performed. Here, this is to be noted: during the twilight worship (*saṃdhyā*), the root goddess’s offerings of water (*arghya*), libations (*tarpaṇa*), and recitations (*japa*) constitute the primary act (*aṅgin*), while the rest are subsidiary acts (*aṅga*). If a subsidiary act is omitted through forgetfulness, there is no requirement to perform it again; rather, its expiation consists of ten recitations of the root mantra. If the primary act is omitted...

If one remembers [the omission] before the second twilight (*saṃdhyā*) has passed, the *saṃdhyā* must be performed again. If one remembers it immediately thereafter, there is the recitation (*japa*) of the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) one hundred and eight times.

This same rule applies even in the case of the complete omission of the *saṃdhyā*. In that regard, in the event of the lapse of the primary time (*mukhya-kāla*), the intermediate time (*madhya-kāla*), or the secondary time (*gauṇa-kāla*), one should respectively recite ten repetitions of the root *Gāyatrī*, one hundred repetitions of the *Gāyatrī* appropriate to that specific time, and one hundred repetitions of the root mantra. The primary time consists of [the periods when] the stars are visible, when the sun is half-set, and when the sun is half-risen.

The morning, midday, and evening twilight periods are primary; the period ending with the second [midday] meal-time is secondary. During the morning twilight, one should face east; during the other two, one should face north. For the offering of *arghya* and for *japa*, one should face the sun. Having thus performed the rites of twilight and so forth, seated upon any one of the seats to be described later in the section on *puraścaraṇa* at the place of recitation, facing either east or north, one should perform the purification of the ground and other preliminary acts.
